newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European feeds stay quiet as dollar dampens trade.
newsitem.headline: European feeds stay quiet as dollar dampens trade.

text.p: European meals and feeds remained thinly traded on Tuesday, shrugging off a firm Chicago close on Monday with the higher dollar helping to keep many consumers sidelined.
"The market in Europe is still very nervous and consumers are continuing to live hand-to-mouth," one trader said.
Traders said most buyers had taken their necessary protection on Monday and were unwilling to buy further ahead.
"They may be willing to pay the premiums for nearbys but are not touching the deferred positions. The consumers are betting on good sized crops this year to push prices lower," one said.

Chicago opened mixed on Tuesday with the market watching for developments in Brazil, where a port strike still loomed. However, activity was not at Monday's levels and workers at the centre of the dispute at the port of Paranagua were due to meet operators to try and avert industrial action.
"The rise yesterday was overdone and certainly the market in Europe doesn't have much confidence in the move," one trader here commented.
